**LESSONS.** Author-intent at HEAD: describe/it + `--spec` as living docs, story→describe→it naming, outside-in ATDD, commit after RED/GREEN/REFACTOR, coordination-not-output mockist boundaries (`552a9a3`), ONE subprocess test, real fixtures, docstrings only on pending specs. Fallout, not style: the four-layer tree and its `__init__.py` contracts (never adopted by the constitution), `describe_bookminder_acceptance`, `describe_bookminder_integration`-in-`e2e/`, `_integration` suffixes, duplicate describes, dead `TEST_HOME`, unit tests of private helpers, `cli.SUPPORTED_FILTERS` patch target (mutated by `fa0bc72` to make RED pass), TODO/story status disagreement. Transferable rules: never let an agent rewrite a rules file wholesale (it fuses history into one un-revertable hunk); a rule's friction is often its function; **"all tests pass, coverage unchanged" cannot validate a change to the tests** — review spec commits by diff, and treat "pure move" as a claim to verify; same `it_` name + weaker assertion is the most dangerous edit in a BDD suite; the patch target is part of the specification; both episodes are one failure — optimizing a meta-artifact against a proxy (readability, tidiness) at the cost of falsifiability, checked by the very apparatus being changed.
